subject: math
title: Picture Graphs, Bar Graphs and Line Plots
seo_title: Grade 2 Picture Graph, Bar Graph and Line Plot Worksheets: Count by 1s, How Many More, Whole-Number Line Plots
standard_text: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths of several objects to the nearest whole unit, or by making repeated measurements of the same object. Show the measurements by making a line plot, where the horizontal scale is marked off in whole-number units. Draw a picture graph and a bar graph (with single-unit scale) to represent a data set with up to four categories. Solve simple put-together, take-apart, and compare problems using information presented in a bar graph.
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 graph worksheets: read picture graphs where each picture is 1, bar graphs that count by 1s and tally charts with up to 4 groups, solve how many in all, how many more and how many fewer, and read whole-number line plots. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Each picture is 1. Each grid line is 1. Each X is 1.
key_sub: Count the pictures in a row, or look straight across from the top of a bar. In all means add; how many more or fewer means subtract. On a line plot, the number under the X's is the length.
body_html:
The big idea

A graph shows data so you can see it fast. In Grade 2, each picture stands for 1 and each grid line on a bar graph counts by 1. A graph can show up to 4 groups.

FruitVotes
Apple6
Banana3
Grape8
Pear4

Picture graph

Each picture is 1 vote. Count the pictures in a row.

Bar graph

Go to the top of the bar. Look across to the numbers. The bar ends at the number of votes.

How many in all? How many more?

In all means put together, so add. How many more or how many fewer means compare, so subtract.

In all

How many votes did Apple and Pear get in all?

Apple 6, Pear 4. 6 + 4 = 10.

Answer: 10 votes

How many more

How many more votes did Grape get than Banana?

Grape 8, Banana 3. 8 − 3 = 5.

Answer: 5 more votes

Line plot

Measure some objects. Draw a number line. Put one X above the length of each object.

Leo measured 10 pencils in inches: 5, 6, 6, 7, 4, 6, 8, 7, 6, 5.

QuestionHow to find itAnswer
How many pencils are 7 inches long?Count the X's above 72
What length are the most pencils?Find the tallest stack6 inches
How many pencils in all?1 + 2 + 4 + 2 + 110

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Reading the bar next to the one you wantPut your finger on the name, then go up the bar
Reading the line just above or belowLook straight across from the top of the bar
Adding when it asks how many moreHow many more or fewer means subtract
Counting the bars instead of the votesAdd the numbers the bars show
On a line plot, giving the number of X's as the lengthThe number under the stack is the length

faq.q: What is a picture graph in 2nd grade?
faq.a: A picture graph uses a small picture for each item, and in 2nd grade each picture stands for 1. Count the pictures in a row to find how many.

faq.q: How do you read a bar graph in 2nd grade?
faq.a: Find the top of the bar and look straight across to the numbers. In 2nd grade each grid line counts by 1, so a bar that stops at 7 shows 7.

faq.q: How do you solve how many more questions with a bar graph?
faq.a: Read the two bars, then subtract the smaller number from the bigger one. If Dog has 8 and Cat has 5, there are 8 − 5 = 3 more dogs.

faq.q: What is a line plot in 2nd grade math?
faq.a: A line plot is a number line with an X above it for each measurement. Students measure objects to the nearest whole inch or centimeter and put one X above each length.

sets.title: Read picture graphs and tally charts

items.q: How many students chose tacos?
items.e: Each circle stands for 1. Count the circles in the Tacos row: 1, 2, 3. So the answer is 3 students.
Each star stands for 1. Count the stars in the Blue row. There are 8. So the answer is 8 votes.

items.q: How many students have a cat?
items.e: Each square stands for 1. Count the squares in the Cat row: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. So the answer is 5 students.
Each heart stands for 1. Count the hearts in the Sam row: 1, 2, 3. So the answer is 3 shells.

items.q: How many students come by car to school?
items.e: Each circle stands for 1. Count the circles in the Car row: 1, 2, 3. So the answer is 3 students.
Each star stands for 1. Count the stars in the Beetle row: 1, 2, 3, 4. So the answer is 4 bugs.

items.q: How many stickers does Kai have?
items.e: Each square stands for 1. Count the squares in the Kai row. There are 9. So the answer is 9 stickers.
Each heart stands for 1. Count the hearts in the Mango row: 1, 2, 3, 4. So the answer is 4 scoops.

items.q: How many votes did Apple get?
items.e: Each circle stands for 1. Count the circles in the Apple row: 1. So the answer is 1 vote.
Each star stands for 1. Count the stars in the Spring row: 1, 2. So the answer is 2 votes.

items.q: Which row shows the most birds?
items.e: Each square is 1, so the row with the most squares wins. Finch has 9. The others have 2, 6, 1.
Each heart is 1, so the row with the fewest hearts wins. Rainy has 1. The others have 3, 4, 6.

items.q: Which row shows 8 students?
items.e: Look for a row with 8 circles. Count the circles in the Swim row. There are 8.
Each star is 1, so the row with the most stars wins. Dolls has 8. The others have 3, 1, 7.

items.q: Which row shows the fewest students?
items.e: Each square is 1, so the row with the fewest squares wins. Popcorn has 1. The others have 9, 3, 6.
Look for a row with 2 hearts. Count the hearts in the Maya row: 1, 2.

items.q: How many students chose salad?
items.e: A group of 4 marks with a line across is 5. The Salad row has 2 groups of 5 and 2 more marks. 5 + 5 + 2 = 12.

items.q: How many votes did Purple get?
items.e: A group of 4 marks with a line across is 5. The Purple row has 2 groups of 5 and 3 more marks. 5 + 5 + 3 = 13.

items.q: How many books did Leo read?
items.e: A group of 4 marks with a line across is 5. The Leo row has 2 groups of 5 and 3 more marks. 5 + 5 + 3 = 13.

items.q: Which row shows the most shells?
items.e: Find the row with the most marks. The Nora row has 2 groups of 5 and 3 more marks. 5 + 5 + 3 = 13. The other rows are Owen 10, Sam 12, Eli 5.

items.q: How many students chose swimming?
items.e: Each grid line is 1 more. The Swim bar ends at the line for 2. So the answer is 2 students.

items.q: How many votes did Pear get?
items.e: Each grid line is 1 more. The Pear bar ends at the line for 3. So the answer is 3 votes.

items.q: How many students ride the bus to school?
items.e: Each grid line is 1 more. The Bus bar ends at the line for 5. So the answer is 5 students.

items.q: How many days were windy?
items.e: The numbers count by 2s, so the line between two numbers is the number in the middle. The Windy bar ends at the line between 4 and 6. That line is 5. So the answer is 5 days.

items.q: How many beetles did the class see?
items.e: Each grid line is 1 more. The Beetle bar ends at the line for 2. So the answer is 2 bugs.

items.q: How many stickers does Lily have?
items.e: The numbers count by 2s, so the line between two numbers is the number in the middle. The Lily bar ends at the line between 4 and 6. That line is 5. So the answer is 5 stickers.

items.q: How many students have a dog?
items.e: Each grid line is 1 more. The Dog bar ends at the line for 2. So the answer is 2 students.

items.q: How many mint scoops were sold?
items.e: The numbers count by 2s, so the line between two numbers is the number in the middle. The Mint bar ends at the line between 4 and 6. That line is 5. So the answer is 5 scoops.

items.q: How many balls are in the bin?
items.e: The numbers count by 2s, so the line between two numbers is the number in the middle. The Balls bar ends at the line between 4 and 6. That line is 5. So the answer is 5 toys.

items.q: How many students chose popcorn?
items.e: Each grid line is 1 more. The Popcorn bar ends at the line for 3. So the answer is 3 students.

items.q: How many votes did Winter get?
items.e: The numbers count by 2s, so the line between two numbers is the number in the middle. The Winter bar ends at the line between 10 and 12. That line is 11. So the answer is 11 votes.

items.q: How many finches came to the feeder?
items.e: The numbers count by 2s, so the line between two numbers is the number in the middle. The Finch bar ends at the line between 2 and 4. That line is 3. So the answer is 3 birds.

items.q: Which bar shows 5 students?
items.e: Find 5 on the numbers. Follow that line across. The Salad bar ends at the line for 5.

items.q: Which bar shows 4 students?
items.e: Find 4 on the numbers. Follow that line across. The Tennis bar ends at the line for 4.

items.q: Which bar shows 1 toy?
items.e: Find 1 on the numbers. Follow that line across. The Blocks bar ends at the line for 1.

items.q: Which bar shows the most books?
items.e: The Ava bar is the longest bar. The Ava bar ends at the line for 9. It shows 9 books.

items.q: Which bar shows the fewest votes?
items.e: The Yellow bar is the shortest bar. The Yellow bar ends at the line for 2. It shows 2 votes.

items.q: Which bar shows the most students?
items.e: The Pretzels bar is the longest bar. The Pretzels bar ends at the line for 7. It shows 7 students.

items.q: Which bar shows the fewest stickers?
items.e: The Emma bar is the shortest bar. The Emma bar ends at the line between 0 and 2. That line is 1. It shows 1 sticker.

items.q: Which two bars show the same number?
items.e: The Pear bar and the Grape bar both end at the line for 6. They are the same length.

sets.title: In all, how many more, how many fewer

items.q: How many vanilla and mango scoops were sold in all?
items.e: Read each bar. Vanilla: 10. Mango: 8. Put them together: 10 + 8 = 18 scoops.

items.q: How many more students have a dog than a bird?
items.e: Read each bar. Dog: 4. Bird: 1. Compare: 4 − 1 = 3. The answer is 3 more students.

items.q: How many fewer shells did Nora find than Mia?
items.e: Read each bar. Mia: 5. Nora: 3. Compare: 5 − 3 = 2. The answer is 2 fewer shells.
Count the pictures in each row. Beetle: 2. Ant: 6. Put them together: 2 + 6 = 8 bugs.

items.q: How many more votes did Spring get than Fall?
items.e: Read each bar. Spring: 6. Fall: 4. Compare: 6 − 4 = 2. The answer is 2 more votes.

items.q: How many fewer days were sunny than cloudy?
items.e: Read each bar. Cloudy: 5. Sunny: 2. Compare: 5 − 2 = 3. The answer is 3 fewer days.

items.q: How many robins and crows came in all?
items.e: Read each bar. Robin: 7. Crow: 3. Put them together: 7 + 3 = 10 birds.
Count the pictures in each row. Car: 7. Walk: 2. Compare: 7 − 2 = 5. The answer is 5 more students.

items.q: How many fewer balls than cars are in the bin?
items.e: Read each bar. Cars: 10. Balls: 7. Compare: 10 − 7 = 3. The answer is 3 fewer toys.

items.q: How many students ride the bus or ride a bike to school?
items.e: Read each bar. Bus: 9. Bike: 4. Put them together: 9 + 4 = 13 students.

items.q: How many more ladybugs than bees did the class see?
items.e: Read each bar. Ladybug: 10. Bee: 7. Compare: 10 − 7 = 3. The answer is 3 more bugs.
Count the pictures in each row. Blue Jay: 7. Crow: 1. Compare: 7 − 1 = 6. The answer is 6 fewer birds.

items.q: How many more votes does Pear need to have as many as Apple?
items.e: Read each bar. Apple: 10. Pear: 5. Pear needs to get from 5 up to 10. 10 − 5 = 5, so Pear needs 5 more votes.

items.q: How many students are shown in all?
items.e: Read each bar. Bird: 7. Fish: 9. Cat: 8. Dog: 4. Add all four: 7 + 9 + 8 + 4 = 28 students. (There are 4 bars, but the answer is the number of students.)

items.q: How many more mint scoops than mango scoops were sold?
items.e: Read each bar. Mint: 5. Mango: 2. Compare: 5 − 2 = 3. The answer is 3 more scoops.
Count the pictures in each row. Yellow: 6. Red: 1. Compare: 6 − 1 = 5. The answer is 5 fewer votes.

items.q: How many votes were not for Spring?
items.e: Leave out Spring. Add the other three: 8 + 5 + 3 = 16 votes.

items.q: How many more books does Maya need to read to have as many as Noah?
items.e: Read each bar. Noah: 9. Maya: 1. Maya needs to get from 1 up to 9. 9 − 1 = 8, so Maya needs 8 more books.

items.q: How many days are shown in all?
items.e: Read each bar. Cloudy: 6. Sunny: 5. Windy: 1. Rainy: 2. Add all four: 6 + 5 + 1 + 2 = 14 days. (There are 4 bars, but the answer is the number of days.)

items.q: How many students did not choose grapes?
items.e: Leave out Grapes. Add the other three: 7 + 6 + 3 = 16 students.

items.q: How many carrots are 7 inches long?
items.e: Find 7 on the number line. Count the X's above it: 2. Each X is one carrot, so 2 carrots are 7 inches long.

items.q: How many toy cars are 7 centimeters long?
items.e: Find 7 on the number line. Count the X's above it: 3. Each X is one toy car, so 3 toy cars are 7 centimeters long.

items.q: How many paper strips are 11 centimeters long?
items.e: Find 11 on the number line. Count the X's above it: 3. Each X is one paper strip, so 3 paper strips are 11 centimeters long.

items.q: How many leaves are 7 inches long?
items.e: Find 7 on the number line. Count the X's above it: 3. Each X is one leaf, so 3 leaves are 7 inches long.

items.q: How many pencils are 4 inches long?
items.e: Find 4 on the number line. Count the X's above it: 3. Each X is one pencil, so 3 pencils are 4 inches long.

items.q: What length are the most shells?
items.e: Find the tallest stack of X's. It is above 4 and has 4 X's. So the most shells are 4 centimeters long. (4 is how many shells, not the length.)

items.q: What length are the most crayons?
items.e: Find the tallest stack of X's. It is above 8 and has 4 X's. So the most crayons are 8 centimeters long. (4 is how many crayons, not the length.)

items.q: What length are the most feathers?
items.e: Find the tallest stack of X's. It is above 4 and has 4 X's. So the most feathers are 4 inches long. (4 is how many feathers, not the length.)

items.q: How many ribbons were measured in all?
items.e: Each X is one ribbon. Count all the X's: 1 + 2 + 3 + 3 + 2 + 4 = 15. (Do not count the numbers on the line.)

items.q: How many sticks were measured in all?
items.e: Each X is one stick. Count all the X's: 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 4 + 3 + 1 = 12. (Do not count the numbers on the line.)

items.q: How many worms were measured in all?
items.e: Each X is one worm. Count all the X's: 3 + 5 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 15. (Do not count the numbers on the line.)

items.q: How long is the longest eraser?
items.e: Find the X that is farthest to the right. It is above 7, so the longest eraser is 7 centimeters. There is no X above 8.

items.q: How long is the shortest carrot?
items.e: Find the X that is farthest to the left. It is above 4, so the shortest carrot is 4 inches. There is no X above 3.

items.q: How many toy cars are longer than 9 centimeters?
items.e: Longer than 9 means more than 9, so do not count the X's above 9. Count the X's to the right of 9: 2 + 2 + 3 = 7.

items.q: How many paper strips are shorter than 11 centimeters?
items.e: Shorter than 11 means less than 11, so do not count the X's above 11. Count the X's to the left of 11: 1 + 1 + 2 = 4.

items.q: How many leaves are longer than 5 inches?
items.e: Longer than 5 means more than 5, so do not count the X's above 5. Count the X's to the right of 5: 3 + 4 + 5 = 12.

items.q: How many more pencils are 8 inches long than 4 inches long?
items.e: Above 8: 4 X's. Above 4: 1 X. 4 − 1 = 3 more pencils.

items.q: How many more shells are 4 centimeters long than 8 centimeters long?
items.e: Above 4: 3 X's. Above 8: 1 X. 3 − 1 = 2 more shells.

items.q: How much longer is the longest crayon than the shortest crayon?
items.e: Longest: 10 centimeters. Shortest: 5 centimeters. 10 − 5 = 5 centimeters. (Count the jumps on the line, not the marks.)

items.q: How much longer is the longest feather than the shortest feather?
items.e: Longest: 8 inches. Shortest: 2 inches. 8 − 2 = 6 inches. (Count the jumps on the line, not the marks.)

sets.title: Make graphs and solve word problems

items.q: Noah measured 10 ribbons in inches: 7, 7, 10, 7, 9, 8, 7, 9, 8, 7. He makes a line plot. How many X's go above 9?
items.e: Put one X for each ribbon. Find every 9 in the list and count them: 2. So 2 X's go above 9.

items.q: Omar measured 11 sticks in inches: 10, 10, 11, 8, 10, 9, 8, 8, 10, 8, 8. He makes a line plot. How many X's go above 10?
items.e: Put one X for each stick. Find every 10 in the list and count them: 4. So 4 X's go above 10.

items.q: Nora measured 12 worms in centimeters: 5, 4, 5, 4, 6, 4, 4, 5, 6, 4, 6, 7. She makes a line plot. How many X's go above 5?
items.e: Put one X for each worm. Find every 5 in the list and count them: 3. So 3 X's go above 5.

items.q: Lily made this bar graph from the data: Baseball 3, Tennis 7, Soccer 9, Swim 5. Which bar is wrong?
items.e: Check each bar against the data. The Tennis bar ends at 8, but the data says 7. It is one line too high.

items.q: Zoe made this bar graph from the data: Nora 3, Eli 9, Sam 6, Mia 7. Which bar is wrong?
items.e: Check each bar against the data. The Nora bar ends at 2, but the data says 3. It is one line too low.

items.q: Leo made this bar graph from the data: Lily 6, Ruby 3, Omar 4, Kai 9. Which bar is wrong?
items.e: Check each bar against the data. The Kai bar ends at 10, but the data says 9. It is one line too high.

items.q: Which bar graph shows this data? Salad 4, Tacos 2, Pizza 5, Pasta 3.
items.e: Check every bar. Only graph C matches: Salad 4, Tacos 2, Pizza 5, Pasta 3. Graph A has Pasta 2; B has Pasta and Salad switched; D has Salad 5.

items.q: Which bar graph shows this data? Leo 5, Ava 3, Zoe 2.
items.e: Check every bar. Only graph A matches: Leo 5, Ava 3, Zoe 2. Graph B has Ava 4; C has Leo 4; D has Zoe and Leo switched.

items.q: Which bar graph shows this data? Pear 2, Grape 3, Peach 1, Apple 4.
items.e: Check every bar. Only graph D matches: Pear 2, Grape 3, Peach 1, Apple 4. Graph A has Pear 3; B has Apple 3; C has Apple and Peach switched.

items.q: Later, 6 more students vote for Green. How many votes does Green have now?
items.e: The Green bar ends at the line for 7. Add the 6 new ones: 7 + 6 = 13 votes.

items.q: Later, 3 more students choose tacos. How many students choose tacos now?
items.e: The Tacos bar ends at the line for 3. Add the 3 new ones: 3 + 3 = 6 students.

items.q: Kai finds 2 more erasers. Each one is 5 centimeters long. He adds them to the line plot. Now how many erasers are 5 centimeters long?
items.e: Right now there are 2 X's above 5. Add 2 more X's: 2 + 2 = 4.

items.q: Jack finds 3 more carrots. Each one is 5 inches long. He adds them to the line plot. Now how many carrots are 5 inches long?
items.e: Right now there is 1 X above 5. Add 3 more X's: 1 + 3 = 4.

items.q: Ava wants to read 12 books this week. How many more books does she need to read?
items.e: The Ava bar ends at the line for 5. Ava has 5 and wants 12. 12 − 5 = 7 more books.

items.q: Mia wants to find 12 shells. How many more shells does she need to find?
items.e: The Mia bar ends at the line for 4. Mia has 4 and wants 12. 12 − 4 = 8 more shells.

items.q: All 20 students in the class are in this graph. The bar for Grapes is missing. How many students chose grapes?
items.e: Add the bars you can see: 2 + 5 + 7 = 14. All 20 students: 20 − 14 = 6 students.

items.q: All 15 students in the class are in this graph. The bar for Dog is missing. How many students have a dog?
items.e: Add the bars you can see: 4 + 6 + 2 = 12. All 15 students: 15 − 12 = 3 students.

items.q: All 24 students in the class are in this graph. The bar for Bike is missing. How many students ride a bike to school?
items.e: Add the bars you can see: 3 + 6 + 8 = 17. All 24 students: 24 − 17 = 7 students.

items.q: How many more birds do the Robin and Blue Jay bars show together than the Crow bar?
items.e: Step 1: Robin + Blue Jay = 4 + 7 = 11. Step 2: compare with Crow (9): 11 − 9 = 2 more birds.

items.q: How many more bugs do the Ant and Ladybug bars show together than the Bee bar?
items.e: Step 1: Ant + Ladybug = 8 + 3 = 11. Step 2: compare with Bee (9): 11 − 9 = 2 more bugs.
